correctness.rationale: A repeated suffix with any one can only be a square, of period d=b+1, with exactly one marker per copy. In zero-based indexing the earliest marker p=a must lie in [t-2d+1,t-d] in a square ending at t, with p+d the other marker. This gives a>=b at the second marker and b>=1,a>=b-1 one step later. Otherwise the terminal zero run supplies the maximum; for runs of length >=2 the possible square cannot increase it. Thus the three-gap factorization is valid. Initial starts 123,121,11 distinguish the stated leading-gap cases; 121 can hide only (2,0,0) versus (0,0,2), and comparison through positions 3–6 in the 11 case gives the other two length-four and the one length-five cross-leading-gap collisions. For fixed a, b=0 is separate, and a staircase of length >=3 gives b uniquely. The local entry index in line 58 is off: for b=1 versus 2 the second entries after R_a(1) agree iff a>=1; the third entries then agree iff a>=2, with the third entries 2 and 1 when a=1. Length equality matches c with c-1. At a>=2 the resulting sequences coincide for c=1,2 and differ at position five after R_a(1) for c>=3. This verifies the claimed pairs despite that indexing slip. Direct n=2,3 cases are injective. The count and uniform conditional entropy and success formulas follow from exactly two doubletons at n>=7.
